scope: Read-only source/log audit and proposed next-iteration regression plan. No production changes, fault injection, model inference or new live trials performed.

observed.sampled_stack: Executor._call finally -> attempt_logger.finished -> FDBToolLogger.finished -> _update_calls -> os.replace (logger line51).
observed.precision: The watchdog reported612.5ms total blocked-loop duration and sampled os.replace81ms into the stall. This is not an isolated measurement that one os.replace call consumed the entire duration.
observed.outcome: The trace and retained attempt rows show search_destination, compute_route and start_navigation all done; original result speech subsequently finished. This stall preceded substantive result speech and the silence probe.
observed.causal_limit: Low reported CPU time is consistent with blocking filesystem/lock work, but does not identify storage, swap, filesystem or scheduler cause. No missed barge-in, failed effect, or worker-shutdown failure is causally attributed to this stall.

current_boundaries.finding: Every start/final update acquires thread and cross-process sidecar locks, rereads all rows, rewrites the full snapshot, fsyncs it, atomically replaces it and fsyncs the directory. The synchronous API is crash-evidence oriented and its work grows with retained history.

TOOL_STARTED emits dispatch intention, then current() is checked. Ledger reservation/protected-write bookkeeping currently precede synchronous started(). Start failure prevents backend entry and aborts the ledger reservation. With no await, a normal loop callback cannot run inside logging today.

Backend entry follows start-log success. Writes are serialized; already-entered writes are protected from corrections. Reads are cancellable; resolved references are validated before reaching this boundary.

Backend outcome and observation end are recorded before synchronous finished(). Protection/write_keys are removed before completion logging. A completion-log failure emits tool_log_error while preserving the actual outcome and existing unconfirmed row.

cancel_stale cancels only unprotected call tasks; aclose marks pending protected writes unknown and has two bounded waits. A naive await inserted before protection moves, or unowned to_thread future, would weaken these guarantees.

The live path supplies FDBToolLogger. Heartbeat append and trace flush are also synchronous, but this evidence samples the attempt logger; moving it alone is not a claim that all loop stalls disappear.

smallest_proposed_change.scope: Retain synchronous FDB snapshot/locking implementation and scorer format. Offload only thread-safe logger I/O through an executor-owned helper; ledger, intent decisions and event emission remain on the event loop. Preserve direct synchronous logger API for existing collectors/tests.
start_sequence: Freeze attempt_id (execution_id:call_id), tool, deep-copied argument payload and intention timestamp on the loop. Retain operation/call argument binding; a pre-I/O ledger reservation is permissible but is not a dispatched write.

Emit dispatch-intention event and retain its synchronous current() check. Submit started() to a tracked worker task and await successful persistence before backend entry. Do not add protected/write_keys until actual dispatch is about to occur.

If a new intent/cancellation arrives while start I/O waits, abort any undispatched ledger reservation immediately, retain identity binding, mark the call cancelled-before-dispatch, and never enter the backend. Cancelling the await cannot stop an already-running disk thread.

Own the surviving start future and its exception. After it succeeds, finalize any cancelled intention as cancelled using the same attempt_id; serialize this finalization after start completion. If start fails or partially persists, emit logging error, preserve remaining evidence and dispatch nothing.

On ordinary start success, perform another current()/closed check. Then set protected/write_keys and invoke the backend without another await or event callback between that final check and entry. Abort/finalize a saved but now-stale intention instead of dispatching it.
finish_sequence: Snapshot immutable attempt_id, executor observation-end timestamp and final status before offloading finished(). Keep done/error/unknown/cancelled distinctions; logging failure must not rewrite backend success.

Remove dispatch protection and write_keys as soon as backend observation ends, as today. Track pending finalization separately so shutdown cannot relabel a completed write unknown merely because disk I/O is slow.

Shield/own finalization work against call/parent cancellation, observe every exception and update the same row exactly once. A queued start must finish before its final row update; existing cross-process locking/atomic replacement remain required.

Include outstanding logger tasks in bounded shutdown accounting. If disk work outlives the deadline, return/report unresolved telemetry and retain owned futures; do not claim a thread was cancelled or the log drained. Never permit late start completion to dispatch after close.
smallest_proposed_change.not_proposed: No fire-and-forget start logging, no post-backend intention write, no shortened durability sequence, no blanket offload of arbitrary event callbacks, no database/append-only migration or new retry policy in this minimal iteration.
smallest_proposed_change.expected_benefit: Disk stalls and lock waits no longer directly monopolize the agent event loop. Required intention persistence still delays its tool dispatch; disk service time, snapshot growth and throughput are not solved by this move.

fault_injection_regression_plan.injection: Hold logger start at a threading.Event barrier before persistence. Use another loop coroutine/event as a deterministic responsiveness witness.
fault_injection_regression_plan.assert: Loop witness runs while backend count remains0. On release, backend itself observes exactly one collectable unconfirmed intention before entry; successful completion updates that same identity.

fault_injection_regression_plan.injection: Freeze a slow start, finalize a newer intent, then release the old disk operation. Repeat for a read and a write.
fault_injection_regression_plan.assert: Old backend never enters; no stale ledger pending/unknown effect remains; any persisted old row is finalized cancelled, operation/call binding remains stable, and the new intended action can execute exactly once.

fault_injection_regression_plan.injection: Schedule a version change at start-future resolution before the post-await version check; retain existing synchronous TOOL_STARTED-sink correction test.
fault_injection_regression_plan.assert: No old backend entry after the final check fails. A persisted intention is visible and cancelled rather than silently removed.

fault_injection_regression_plan.injection: Raise before writing and after atomic replacement but before successful directory-fsync return.
fault_injection_regression_plan.assert: No backend effect in either case, explicit tool_log_error, no uncertain backend ledger entry; partial unconfirmed disk evidence remains visible. Retrying a valid intentional operation is not accidentally blocked by an undispatched reservation.

fault_injection_regression_plan.injection: Block finished() after backend success, issue a correction and repeated shutdown cancellation, then release I/O.
fault_injection_regression_plan.assert: Done ledger/outcome stays done, no fabricated unknown write, same attempt identity eventually receives done/end timestamp, and all exceptions are observed.

fault_injection_regression_plan.injection: Exercise explicit backend rejection, lost-ack write exception, cancelled read, already-dispatched superseded write, and completion logger failure.
fault_injection_regression_plan.assert: Existing error/unknown/cancelled/done outcomes and every attempt remain intact; completion failure leaves an unconfirmed row plus visible logging error without converting successful effects to failures.

fault_injection_regression_plan.injection: Mutate caller-owned argument containers after submission and interleave rooms with overlapping call IDs plus existing cross-process logger updates.
fault_injection_regression_plan.assert: Persisted and dispatched arguments use the frozen attempt payload; exactly one row per unique execution/call attempt, no clobbered rows, and existing unmodified upstream collection still works.

fault_injection_regression_plan.injection: Hold a worker I/O barrier beyond both shutdown windows; release only after aclose reports unresolved work.
fault_injection_regression_plan.assert: Event loop remains responsive, aclose returns within its bound and reports incomplete cleanup, late logger success cannot dispatch a closed/stale action, and finalization/error callbacks are retained. Do not claim Python can forcibly stop the disk thread.

acceptance: Run new fault-injection tests against the baseline first, preserve failures, implement the minimal boundary-safe change, then targeted telemetry/executor/correction tests and the full suite. A separate predeclared slow-disk RTC comparison is needed before claiming improved live interruption latency.
